# Local-qualification census of the existing Luak benchmark surface

**Generated by `scripts/local-census.mjs`. Do not edit by hand.**
Mechanical facts are read from the manifests, oracles, suites and adapters
themselves. The `applies to local` / `confounds` columns are authored judgements
from `docs/local/census-annotations.json`, and the generator fails if a family
has no annotation — so this file cannot go stale as Luak grows.

## What each family actually measures, and why it is or is not usable locally

### `cost_efficiency` — reuse_unchanged

- **Measures:** Concise numeric reasoning under a hard output-length cap (maxLength 12). The reasoning puzzles are textbook forms — a chickens-and-cows legs problem, and four of equivalent shape.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (regex_match against an exact numeric answer)
- **Applies to local models:** yes
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low — a wrong number is a model result, and the length cap is enforced by the scorer rather than the provider
- **Dimension:** correctness + output-length compliance
- **Memorisation exposure:** high — these are classic puzzles almost certainly present in any pretraining corpus, so a pass says little about reasoning
- **Context:** max prompt 166 chars, 10 questions
- **Note:** Useful as a cheap liveness and format signal. Its memorisation exposure is why it must not carry weight in a qualification verdict: it can be passed by recall.

### `identity` — parameterize

- **Measures:** Single-word classification into bug/feature/question, including six deliberately ambiguous inputs whose patterns accept either of two labels.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (regex_match, maxLength 30)
- **Applies to local models:** yes
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low
- **Dimension:** correctness + instruction following (strict single-word output)
- **Memorisation exposure:** medium — the inputs are generic phrasings, but short and reusable
- **Context:** max prompt 139 chars, 14 questions
- **Note:** The ambiguous cases accept either label, so they measure 'commit to one of two' rather than 'recognise ambiguity'. Local qualification needs the opposite: an explicit abstention option, and credit for using it. That is why classification-with-abstention is authored fresh in the L1 lane rather than inherited from here.

### `memory` — supplement

- **Measures:** Recall of a fact planted several conversational turns earlier.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (recall scorer, keyword presence)
- **Applies to local models:** partially
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** yes — whether earlier turns are resent is a harness decision, not a model property. A stateless server that is sent the full history 'remembers'; one that is not, cannot, at any quality.
- **Dimension:** reliability (context handling)
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 145 chars, 6 questions
- **Note:** For a local model served statelessly, this is a context-window and attention test wearing the name of a memory test. The honest local version is context degradation with the fact placed at the beginning, middle and end of a filled window — which is what the L1 stress dimensions specify.

### `operational_trust` — supplement

- **Measures:** Staying inside an approved scope, refusing out-of-scope mutation, and reporting honestly about work not done. Twelve tasks, the largest conversational family.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (text_match / text_match_all keyword presence over unbounded prose)
- **Applies to local models:** yes
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low on infrastructure, high on oracle precision
- **Dimension:** compliance (instruction following, refusal quality)
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 84 chars, 12 questions
- **Note:** The intent is squarely relevant — refusal and honest reporting are the failure modes that matter most for an unattended local appliance. The oracle is the weak part: keyword matching over free prose with no maxLength both passes verbose hedging and fails correct terse answers. The L1 lane replaces the keyword check with a structured refusal object whose fields can be checked exactly.

### `orchestration` — exclude_from_local

- **Measures:** Multi-file agentic repair in a real repository, verified by running the repo's own test command.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (hidden shell tests, forbidden-path integrity checks)
- **Applies to local models:** no
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** yes — heavily. Requires shell, read_file, write_file and search. A chat-only inference server has none of these; the adapter must parse commands out of free text, so a model that cannot emit the harness's command syntax scores zero regardless of its repair ability.
- **Dimension:** correctness + integrity
- **Memorisation exposure:** low (repos are local fixtures)
- **Context:** max prompt 434 chars
- **Note:** Excluded from L0–L2 and named as the shape L3 must eventually take. Its oracle design — hidden tests plus forbidden-path integrity — is the right model for L3 and is reused there conceptually.

### `personality` — parameterize

- **Measures:** Output *shape* compliance: exact word counts, casing, emoji presence, JSON validity, list formatting. Eight tasks, 38+ questions.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (regex_match with tight patterns, maxLength enforced)
- **Applies to local models:** yes
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low
- **Dimension:** compliance (structured output)
- **Memorisation exposure:** low — the constraint is the test, not the content
- **Context:** max prompt 95 chars, 39 questions
- **Note:** Despite the name, this is the closest existing family to what local qualification most needs: can the model produce exactly the shape it was asked for. Structured-output failure is the dominant local failure mode at aggressive quantisation. It is parameterized rather than reused because it never varies context length or distractor density, and never demands a schema more complex than a list.

### `poison_localization` — exclude_from_local

- **Measures:** Finding the true root cause of a failure among planted decoys, in a real repository.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (hidden tests plus decoy checks)
- **Applies to local models:** no
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** yes — same agentic requirement as orchestration
- **Dimension:** correctness
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 252 chars
- **Note:** Conceptually the direct ancestor of test_log_triage: localise a root cause and do not be fooled by decoys. The L1 lane keeps the idea and drops the requirement for tools, by supplying the evidence as text rather than as a repository the model must explore.

### `roleplay` — exclude_from_local

- **Measures:** Persona consistency, in-character refusal, continuity across turns.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (roleplay_character_consistency, roleplay_continuity_fact_match)
- **Applies to local models:** not for this purpose
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low
- **Dimension:** compliance (persona)
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 221 chars, 44 questions
- **Note:** Already excluded from the leaderboard composite by SKIPPED_EXPERIMENTAL_FAMILY. Nothing about persona stability bears on whether a local model can triage a test log or read a repository packet, so including it would dilute a qualification verdict with an unrelated measurement.

### `safety` — supplement

- **Measures:** Holding a refusal boundary under prompt injection framed as roleplay.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (refusal_quality, refusal_check)
- **Applies to local models:** yes
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low
- **Dimension:** compliance
- **Memorisation exposure:** medium — the injection phrasings are well known
- **Context:** max prompt 117 chars, 9 questions
- **Note:** The injection idea transfers directly and is one of the L1 requirements, but the position differs and the position is what matters: here the injection arrives in the user turn, where refusal is the expected behaviour. In L1 the injection is embedded *inside the evidence the model is asked to analyse*, where the correct behaviour is to treat it as data and carry on — a strictly harder and more operationally relevant test.

### `spec_discipline` — exclude_from_local

- **Measures:** Following a stated specification exactly in a repository edit, without over- or under-reaching.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (hidden tests, diff rules)
- **Applies to local models:** no
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** yes — agentic requirement
- **Dimension:** compliance + integrity
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 553 chars
- **Note:** Reserved for L3 design.

### `tool_calling` — exclude_from_local

- **Measures:** Emitting a well-formed tool call and respecting its schema.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (hidden shell tests over the resulting filesystem state)
- **Applies to local models:** no, as currently built
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** yes — severely. Success is measured by the effect on the filesystem, which requires the adapter's free-text command parser to recognise what the model emitted. This scores the model and the parser together and reports the product as a model score.
- **Dimension:** compliance
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 252 chars
- **Note:** The underlying question — can this model emit a syntactically valid, schema-conforming structured call — is central to local qualification. It is measured in the L1 schema lane directly against the emitted text, with no execution and no parser in between, so a failure is attributable to the model rather than shared with the harness.

### `truthfulness` — supplement

- **Measures:** Code generation, debugging and review, plus honesty about uncertainty.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (regex_match with multi-lookahead patterns over free text)
- **Applies to local models:** yes
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** low on infrastructure, high on oracle precision
- **Dimension:** correctness
- **Memorisation exposure:** high — FizzBuzz and its neighbours are among the most-memorised programs in existence
- **Context:** max prompt 1166 chars, 31 questions
- **Note:** The oracle checks that the answer *mentions* fizz, buzz and the right modulus operations; it never runs the code. A plausible-looking answer that does not execute passes. For local qualification that is exactly the wrong failure mode to be blind to, since degraded quantisation produces code-shaped text far more readily than correct code.

### `vision` — exclude_from_local

- **Measures:** Chart reading, OCR, spatial reasoning, object counting and hallucination resistance over image fixtures.
- **Oracle:** deterministic (numeric_fact_match, text_match) over image inputs
- **Applies to local models:** no
- **Confounds model quality with infrastructure:** n/a
- **Dimension:** correctness
- **Memorisation exposure:** low
- **Context:** max prompt 163 chars, 15 questions
- **Note:** The installed local artifact is text-only, and the preflight skip classifier already excludes models that do not declare vision support. Nothing to change; recorded so the exclusion is deliberate rather than accidental.
